name: FaultyTerminal-TS-TW

frames.best_why: A dense green glyph cloud fills the upper half behind the title, showing the CRT grid clearly.

tagline: Green glyphs flicker into cloudy shapes on a black CRT grid.
summary: A full-screen green terminal grid of tiny glyphs that clump into drifting cloud shapes, with scanlines, flicker and noise, plus a cursor that brightens a ripple near it.
appearance: Black filled with a fine grid of tiny pale-green glyphs and squares, clustering into soft clouds and bands so the surface reads like a malfunctioning terminal display. White text sits over the centre, and faint scanlines and curvature suggest a curved CRT screen.
behaviour: The green glyph clusters drift and flicker, with sections cutting out and returning as the noise field moves. Moving the cursor adds a bright ripple around the pointer, and a load animation fades the grid in from the edges.
demo_content: A white heading 'System failure' with the line 'A glitching CRT grid that reacts to the cursor.'
use_when: You want a cyberpunk or error-state backdrop that suggests a broken screen behind an alert or 404.
avoid_when: The busy green grid and flicker make body text hard to read, and the effect runs continuously.
customise: Props set scale, grid multiplier, digit size, time scale, pause, scanlines, glitch, flicker, noise, chromatic aberration, dither, curvature, tint, brightness, mouse reaction and its strength.
weight_why: A full-screen WebGL shader with layered noise, glyph, scanline and glitch passes every frame.

a11y.note: The glitch and flicker run constantly and ignore reduced-motion, which can be uncomfortable; the canvas has no label.

issues: Constant flicker and glitch can be uncomfortable and ignore reduced-motion.
The dense green glyphs make the small overlaid tagline hard to read.
The busy grid would overwhelm any body text placed on top of it.
polish_why: Convincing broken-CRT texture, but the dense flicker is busy and the subtitle is hard to read.
title: Faulty Terminal
